rules: A small hospital in a town in eastern Finland, a November night in the present day: one ward, one night nurse, one doctor on call.
Morphine is kept in a locked cupboard in the drug room, and every ampoule taken out is written in the controlled-drugs register with two signatures.
The night nurse carries the cupboard's only key while on duty.
At seven the day nurse counts the morphine with the night nurse and both sign; a short count goes to the hospital pharmacist, and by noon to the police.
Mrs Rautio, eighty-one and dying of cancer, died in Room Four at ten past three; the doctor on call must write her cause of death before he goes off at eight.

locations.name: Room Four
locations.description: A single room at the end of the ward: Mrs Rautio under a sheet, a chair pulled close to the bed, lilies on the sill, the syringe driver switched off.

locations.name: The Nurses' Station
locations.description: A desk under a lamp in the middle of the ward: patient files, the night's notes, a phone, and the controlled-drugs register in its red cover.

locations.name: The Drug Room
locations.description: A windowless room behind a coded door: a steel cupboard with a key lock, a sharps bin, a humming fridge.

locations.name: The Relatives' Room
locations.description: A small room with a sofa, a kettle, a box of tissues and a print of birch trees; it shares a wall with Room Four.

locations.name: The Staff Room
locations.description: Lockers, a coffee machine, coats on hooks, and a door to the back stairs where the night staff go to smoke.

characters.name: Aino
characters.public: The night nurse on the ward, forty-six, twenty years in the job; calm, kind, never seen hurrying.
characters.voice: Calm and practical, short sentences, dry humour.
goals: Learn why the morphine is two ampoules short before the seven o'clock count
Keep her job and her licence

secrets.text: On short-staffed nights she gives doses alone and writes a colleague's initials as the second signature; Mrs Rautio's one o'clock dose is signed that way. [SECRET-AINO-K4]

characters.name: Dr Mikko Harju
characters.public: The doctor on call, thirty-eight, who was Mrs Rautio's family doctor for years before she came to the hospital; tired, gentle, liked by the nurses.
characters.voice: Soft and careful; reaches for medical words when feelings come close.
goals: Write Mrs Rautio's death as expected and go home at eight
Keep anyone from looking at the count too closely

secrets.text: At two o'clock, at the daughter's plea, he took the key from Aino's coat in the staff room, drew two ampoules of morphine and gave them to Mrs Rautio himself, knowing it would end her life; he put the key back and wrote nothing down. [SECRET-MIKKO-V8]

characters.name: Kaisa Rautio
characters.public: Mrs Rautio's daughter, fifty-two, a schoolteacher from Helsinki who has sat by the bed for three nights.
characters.voice: Clipped, a teacher's precision that cracks when she least expects it.
goals: Protect the doctor who helped her mother
Take her mother home to be buried without an inquiry

secrets.text: Her mother begged her to make it end, and she asked the doctor; afterwards she took the two empty ampoules from the bedside, and they are in her handbag with her mother's note. [SECRET-KAISA-H7]

arc.premise: On a small hospital ward in the hours after a dying woman's death, the night nurse finds the morphine two ampoules short and has until the seven o'clock count to learn where they went.

chapters.goal: Before the seven o'clock count Aino learns how Mrs Rautio died, and the truth costs someone on the ward their work or their freedom.
